reasons: No test is visible that pins the threshold at 100 percent or the tolerance values.
The file holds no logic, so its risk is in the values it sets.

terms.meaning: a number that can be linked either to a stored calculation or to a source passage
the minimum share of numbers that must be traceable for the gate to pass

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Engine name and version
sections.what: Names the gate and gives it a version number, which the header says must change whenever its behavior changes.
sections.why: Stored records are keyed by this version, so two measurements from different behavior are not mixed up.
sections.watch_out: If behavior changes without a version bump, old and new results look like the same measurement.

sections.name: E25_THRESHOLD
sections.title: Threshold with a version tag
sections.what: Sets the required traceable rate to 100 percent and attaches a version tag to it.
sections.why: The comment says the tag stops a lowered bar from looking like an improvement.
sections.watch_out: If the number changes, the tag must change too, or reports will look comparable when they are not.

sections.name: E25_MATCH_TOLERANCE, NumeralClass
sections.title: Matching tolerance and classes
sections.what: Sets how close a number must be to its source, at half a percent or an absolute amount, and names the four classes a numeral can take.
sections.why: The comment says the tolerance covers rounding in displayed numbers.
sections.watch_out: Loosening the tolerance makes more numbers match, which raises the rate without any change in the evidence.

sections.name: UntraceableCause
sections.title: Reasons a number is untraceable
sections.what: Lists the four reasons a number can fail: no evidence row, evidence without a passage, a passage that does not contain the number, and a derived number with no calculation record.
sections.why: The header says these are exactly the four causes the brief asks for.
sections.watch_out: A new cause must be added here and in the list below, or the report will not count it.

sections.name: UNTRACEABLE_CAUSES
sections.title: Ordered list of untraceable causes
sections.what: Lists the same four causes in a fixed order, used when the report counts each one.
sections.why: Likely reason: it makes the report show a count for every cause, even when the count is zero.
sections.watch_out: This list must match the type above exactly, or some causes will be missing from the report.

sections.name: ClaimKind
sections.title: Kinds of claim an artifact can make
sections.what: Defines the four claim kinds: derived, reported, client supplied, and unknown.
sections.why: The header says claims made by artifacts are not trusted, only checked.
sections.watch_out: The claim kind chosen by each extractor decides which check the validator runs.

sections.name: UnitHint
sections.title: Unit hints
sections.what: Defines the labels for how a number's unit relates to the way sources usually write it.
sections.why: Lets matching try equivalent units, such as millions of dollars against full dollars.
sections.watch_out: A wrong hint can cause a false match or a false miss.

sections.name: EvidenceLookup
sections.title: Evidence lookup shape
sections.what: Defines a lookup as a project plus a list of field names used to find evidence rows.
sections.why: The header explains that artifacts usually do not carry evidence IDs for single values.
sections.watch_out: The field names must use the same normalized form the renderer uses, or no rows are found.

sections.name: NumeralClaim
sections.title: Numeral claim shape
sections.what: Defines one number an artifact emitted: its address, label, value, display form, kind, any linked computation or evidence IDs, lookup, inline quote, unit hint, and year flag.
sections.why: This is the shape the validator reads for each number.
sections.watch_out: The inline quote is for information only and is never counted as proof of a source.

sections.name: IndexedEvidence
sections.title: Evidence snapshot shape
sections.what: Defines the snapshot of one evidence row: its class, whether it has a URL, whether it was client supplied, and its source passages.
sections.why: The validator needs this data without touching the database.
sections.watch_out: Client supplied status is inferred only from a missing URL.

sections.name: IndexedComputation
sections.title: Computation snapshot shape
sections.what: Defines the snapshot of one calculation record: its ID, field path, engine, and stored value.
sections.why: Derived numbers are checked against this stored value.
sections.watch_out: The stored value may be empty, and the validator must handle that case.

sections.name: ProvenanceIndex, ArtifactMode
sections.title: Snapshot bundle and artifact modes
sections.what: Bundles the evidence and computation snapshots together, and defines the three modes of off, warn, and block.
sections.why: Keeps everything the validator needs in one object.
sections.watch_out: Mode values must match the ones used in the modes file.

sections.name: ArtifactRef
sections.title: Artifact reference
sections.what: Defines the artifact's ID and kind, and optionally the run it belongs to.
sections.why: The optional run lets the saved record link to the run that produced the artifact.
sections.watch_out: If the run ID is empty, the saved record cannot link back to a run.

sections.name: ClassifiedNumeral
sections.title: Result for one number
sections.what: Defines the result for a single number: its class, the reason if untraceable, which record matched, and a plain explanation.
sections.why: The explanation is what a person reads when checking a report.
sections.watch_out: The comment says an explanation is always given for untraceable numbers, so that field should not be empty for them.

sections.name: E25Counts
sections.title: Count summary
sections.what: Defines the five counts: total numbers, computed, sourced, client supplied, and untraceable.
sections.why: Gives a quick summary of the report.

sections.name: E25Report
sections.title: Full report shape
sections.what: Defines the whole report: counts, rates, distance from the threshold, pass or fail, whether it would block, whether it is enforced, and tallies by cause and by label.
sections.why: The comment says the report gives a rate and distance, never a bare pass or fail.
sections.watch_out: The enforced flag is true only in block mode, and no artifact is in block mode today.

summary: Defines the shared vocabulary of the provenance gate: its name, version, threshold, claim kinds, input shapes, and report shape, with no logic of its own.
purpose: Gives the checker, the database layer, and the extractors one shared set of words, so they do not need to import each other.
why: The header says the file holds only types and constants for this reason.
how: Sets the engine name and version, the threshold and its tag, the matching tolerance, and the four classes. Then defines the input and output shapes used by the other files.
inputs: None. This file is read by other files.
risks: Changing the engine version or threshold tag affects how stored records are grouped. Changing the tolerance changes which numbers match.
debug: If a report shows an unexpected threshold or version, check the tag and version constants first.
